summary: Regression + bug-fix verification of COOKIE_SECURE env-driven Set-Cookie behavior for RelayLab. All 11 review points validated. Default (unset/false) omits the `Secure` attribute on rl_session; truthy variants (1/true/yes/on, case-insensitive) add it; falsy/garbage values do not. Login/logout cycle works end-to-end with cookie jar. Delete-cookie on logout mirrors the current secure flag. Full pytest suite 110/110 GREEN.

verification_matrix.T4_truthy_falsy_matrix: PASS — truthy: 1, yes, on, TRUE => Secure PRESENT; falsy: 0, no, False, garbage, '' => Secure ABSENT

verification_matrix.T6_logout_secure_flag_match: PASS — with COOKIE_SECURE=true logout Set-Cookie has Secure; with false it does not. Follow-up /me returns 401.

NOTE: a yarn.lock file DOES currently exist at /app/frontend/yarn.lock (Emergent-generated); Dockerfile intentionally ignores it, so container builds still work either way.

(custom hostname)`

critical_code_review_comments: Minor: /app/frontend/yarn.lock IS committed in the workspace, contradicting the Dockerfile comment 'yarn.lock is intentionally NOT committed'. This is not a functional issue (Dockerfile only copies package.json), but the comment/README should be aligned with reality — either commit-and-use lockfile with --frozen-lockfile, or gitignore it. Leaving as-is is safe.
Minor style: _cookie_secure() re-imports `os as _os` inside the function; could be moved to module-level for micro-perf, but negligible.
routes.py is 1466 lines (>700 threshold) — recommend future split into submodules (auth, master-data, work-orders, qc, uploads). Not blocking.

context_for_next_testing_agent: COOKIE_SECURE default restored to `false` in /app/backend/.env at end of testing; backend restarted. All 110 pytest cases green. Fix behaves exactly as designed; no regressions. Only nit is that /app/frontend/yarn.lock exists despite the Dockerfile comment saying it isn't committed — cosmetic only.
rca of the issue: Original bug: response.set_cookie(secure=True) was hardcoded in /api/auth/login. Browsers refuse to send Secure cookies over plain HTTP for non-localhost origins (custom hostname like http://relaylab-production), so subsequent requests carried no rl_session cookie and backend returned {"detail":"Belum login"}. Fix: introduced _cookie_secure() helper reading COOKIE_SECURE env (default false), applied to both set_cookie in login and delete_cookie in logout; wired through docker-compose.yml and .env.example; documented in README_DEPLOY_WINDOWS.md. Verified via curl -si that the `Secure` attribute now toggles correctly with the env var while HttpOnly/SameSite=lax/Path/Max-Age remain unchanged.
